tools.name: share_text
tools.description: Use this when another AI agent, chat session or person needs text you have: instructions, code, JSON, a prompt for another model. Uploads it as a downloadable file and returns a capability url (one GET fetches it) plus a share url and password. No account or API key needed.

tools.name: share_file
tools.description: Use this when another AI agent (a different machine, model or chat session) or a person needs access to one or more files. Accepts text or base64-encoded binary content; multiple files are zipped into one bundle server-side, so a whole handoff (instructions plus code plus data) travels as one capabi

tools.name: share_conversation
tools.description: Use this to hand your full working context to another AI: any provider, any model, any chat client. Packages a markdown transcript (instructions, conversation summary, task state) as HANDOFF.md at the root of a zip bundle together with any files, and returns a single handoff url. The receiving model

tools.name: receive_file
tools.description: Use this when you have been given an 83blue link and need the file. Accepts a capability url (https://upload.83blue.com/f/...) on its own, or a share url plus password. Returns metadata including sha256, the file list for zip bundles, and the content inline when it is text within max_inline_bytes; o

tools.name: deploy_site
tools.description: Use this to put a static website you have built (HTML, CSS, JS, images, fonts) onto the public web in one call, with no signup, no account and no config. Give it the files (there must be an index.html at the root) and it returns a live https url, e.g. https://upload.83blue.com/s/brave-otter-482/, pl

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: Return the status, address, size and expiry of a site you deployed. Pass the url, host or slug.

tools.name: delete_site
tools.description: Remove a site you deployed. Needs the site url/host/slug and its manage_key (returned by deploy_site).

tools.name: remember
tools.description: Durable cross-session memory for AI agents: store notes, context, text or JSON now and recall it in a later session or from another machine by url. A free cloud scratchpad and shared key-value store for agents, no signup, no account, no API key. Also callable as save_memory, store_memory, save_note,

tools.name: recall
tools.description: Fetch back durable memory, or any shared file/text, by its 83blue url or token (a capability url, or a share url plus password). Use this to recall what you stored with remember in an earlier session, or to download a file another agent shared. Also callable as get_memory, download_file, fetch_file,

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: share_text, share_conversation, receive_file, list_sites, remember, recall · Private data: share_text, share_file, share_conversation, receive_file, deploy_site, remember, recall · Public sink: share_text, share_file, share_conversation, receive_file, deploy_site, recall · Destructive: deploy_site, delete_site.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: share_text, share_conversation, receive_file, list_sites, remember, recall · Private data: share_text, share_file, share_conversation, receive_file, deploy_site, remember, recall · Public sink: share_text, share_file, share_conversation, receive_file, deploy_site, recall · Destructive: deploy_site, delete_site

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "receive_file" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
